data: Long March 7 pad on Hainan: all ten Tianzhou cargo ships to Tiangong, plus Long March 8 flights

Launch Complex 201 is the second of three pads at the Wenchang Space Launch Site on Hainan, built for the Long March 7 and also used by the Long March 7A and Long March 8. The first launch from the site, and from this pad, was the Long March 7 maiden flight on 25 June 2016 (12:00 UTC) with the Yuanzheng-1A upper stage. All ten Tianzhou cargo ships to the Tiangong station launched from LC-201, from Tianzhou 1 on 20 April 2017 to Tianzhou 10 on 11 May 2026. Sources: Wikipedia (Wenchang Space Launch Site, Long March 7, Tianzhou), Astronautix, SpacePolicyOnline; coordinates from Wikipedia.
China's new Wenchang space launch site ready for action — SpacePolicyOnline

LC-201 is the second of Wenchang's three pads, on the north-east coast of Hainan at 19.6 degrees north. It was built for the Long March 7, which made its maiden flight from here on 25 June 2016 with the Yuanzheng-1A upper stage, which released small satellites in several orbits. That was the first launch from the whole site; the Long March 5 followed from LC-101 on 3 November 2016. Tianzhou 1, the first Chinese automated cargo ship, left LC-201 on 20 April 2017, and all ten Tianzhou ships flown through 11 May 2026 launched from this pad to the Tiangong station. The Long March 8 first flew from LC-201 on 22 December 2020 and carried the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite on 20 March 2024. Rockets reach Wenchang by sea, through its own seaport.
